scope: PATH-01 configuration diff preview: read-only old/new value comparison, command-entry drift, PATH resolution and package-impact note before any write
status: implemented-and-isolated-ui-verified; real manager configuration write and real registry comparison not performed
implementation: pkgtools::preview_tool_config reuses the same catalog checks, layout validation and target computation as apply_tool_config, but performs no write
ToolConfigPreview carries changes (key, role, current, next), blocked reasons, warnings, command entry drift, merged-PATH resolution and a package-impact flag
build_config_changes is pure so fixtures compare arbitrary old/new manager values without touching the registry
role_for_key classifies global/command/cache/configuration keys across npm, pnpm, Yarn Classic/Berry, pip, uv, pipx, bun, cargo and composer
config_target_exists/config_target_non_empty only inspect targets: a missing target is reported, never created
preview lists unchanged values as well, so a user can see the final target even when nothing changes
preview adds a warning when the target entry is shadowed by a path-earlier installation and when a non-empty target already exists
preview_blocked mirrors the write path: unsupported capabilities, invalid layout, missing/unusable manager executable, and Yarn 2+ global configuration
the UI opens a confirmation dialog from 仅设置路径 that shows the diff first; 写入配置 stays disabled while preview.blocked is non-empty
npm run verify coverage: packages-ui asserts that preview is called before apply, that no apply call happens while previewing, and that a blocked preview never applies

uiCoverage.previewBeforeWrite: 仅设置路径 calls preview_tool_config and leaves apply_tool_config uncalled until 写入配置 is pressed
uiCoverage.diffRender: old value, new value, unset old value, command-entry change marker, non-empty target warning and shadowed resolution are asserted
uiCoverage.blockedPath: a pip preview with a blocked reason keeps 写入配置 disabled and never calls apply_tool_config

notVerified: No real package-manager configuration was changed; the preview ran only through fixtures and a simulated UI backend
The current-value side of the diff is read through the manager's own query commands, which were not compared against a real installation in this round
limitations: Preview lists configuration keys and the computed command entry; it does not enumerate every global package that would be affected
Unchanged values are included intentionally so the user still sees the final target; the UI does not currently highlight which rows actually change
The command-entry change is reported but old entries are not removed automatically
